text: dsh-safemode-profile 是面向 DSH CLI 与 Web profile 的配置守护插件。它作为 Cordis 插件行启动，在 DSH 加载时创建或还原 safemode profile，并用默认核心 bundle 白名单重写配置；用户也可通过 DSH_SAFEMODE_BUNDLES 指定列表。运行期间，它监听受管配置文件变化并定时检查漂移，发现 bundle、依赖或 patch 层偏离模板时自动恢复。另提供手动还原脚本，适合需要启动隔离 profile 并保持配置一致的 DSH 用户。需要 Node.js 18 或更新版本，不需要 API 密钥或外部账号。

dsh-safemode-profile restores DSH safemode files to a core bundle whitelist at startup. DSH_SAFEMODE_BUNDLES overrides the list. A watcher and periodic check detect drift and restore changed bundles, dependencies, or patch settings. Includes a restore tool. Requires Node.js 18+; no API key needed.
想让 DSH 启动一个只加载指定核心 bundle 的独立 profile。
DSH 的 safemode 配置被改乱了，能不能启动时自动恢复？
我想自定义安全 profile 允许加载哪些 bundle。
有没有办法在运行时发现 profile 文件变化后自动还原？
不重启 DSH 时，怎样立即把 safemode profile 写回模板？
让 DSH 定期检查插件白名单和 patch 配置有没有漂移。
I want DSH to recreate its safemode profile with a fixed bundle whitelist on startup.
Can DSH watch profile files and restore the expected configuration when they change?
dsh-safemode-profile 的功能「启动时还原」：启动时将 safemode 的配置文件写回白名单模板，默认保留两个核心 bundle，也可通过环境变量覆盖。
dsh-safemode-profile 的功能「持续检测并还原」：运行期间监听 profile 目录中的受管文件变更，并每 30 秒比较一次模板；检测到漂移后会重新写入白名单配置。
dsh-safemode-profile 的功能「手动立即还原」：用户可运行随包提供的 ensure-safemode.mjs 脚本，立即创建或恢复 safemode profile，并在终端看到创建、恢复或已符合模板的结果。

```
dsh --profile safemode        # 零第三方插件启动（建议: dsh --profile safemode --port 3081）
```

都不能阻止**删除**文件（删除取决于父目录权限，root 更是无视一切权限位）。
以下两种是"**强锁**"，按需选择：

text: dsh-safemode-profile README · Windows：ACL 拒绝（icacls）——可精确到"写"与"删"：```powershell
section: Windows：ACL 拒绝（icacls）——可精确到"写"与"删"

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · 拒绝当前用户对三个文件的写入（W=写数据）：icacls "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\safemode\package.json" /deny "$env:USERNAME:(W)"
icacls "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\safemode\cordis.patch.yml" /deny "$env:USERNAME:(W)"
icacls "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\safemode\pnpm-workspace.yaml" /deny "$env:USERNAME:(W)"
section: 拒绝当前用户对三个文件的写入（W=写数据）

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · 更进一步：连删除也拒绝（DE=删除；WD=写数据/创建文件）：icacls "...\package.json" /deny "$env:USERNAME:(WD,DE)"
```

解除（删除该用户的 deny 条目）：

```powershell
icacls "...\package.json" /remove:d "$env:USERNAME"
```

要点：
- `(W)` 挡内容修改，`(DE)` 挡删除，`(WD)` 挡写+创建——比 attrib 更精确，
  可以只挡写入、保留"管理员能删"的余地；
- **仍挡不住管理员**：Administrators / SYSTEM 默认有完全控制（F），
  管理员可以夺回所有权或清除 deny。要连管理员一起挡，需对
  `BUILTIN\Administrators` 也加 deny，但管理员仍能通过"取得所有权"绕开；
- icacls 需要对该文件有修改 ACL 的权限（文件所有者默认有）。
section: 更进一步：连删除也拒绝（DE=删除；WD=写数据/创建文件）

section: Linux：immutable 属性（chattr +i）——root 也动不了

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · 加锁：文件不可修改、不可删除、不可改名（包括 root）：sudo chattr +i ~/.dsh/profiles/safemode/package.json \
              ~/.dsh/profiles/safemode/cordis.patch.yml \
              ~/.dsh/profiles/safemode/pnpm-workspace.yaml
section: 加锁：文件不可修改、不可删除、不可改名（包括 root）

text: dsh-safemode-profile README · 查看：lsattr ~/.dsh/profiles/safemode/package.json     # 输出含 i 即已锁定
section: 查看

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · 解锁：sudo chattr -i ~/.dsh/profiles/safemode/package.json \
              ~/.dsh/profiles/safemode/cordis.patch.yml \
              ~/.dsh/profiles/safemode/pnpm-workspace.yaml
```

要点：
- `+i`（immutable）是最强锁：**任何人（含 root）都不能改、删、改名**，
  必须先 `-i` 才能操作——比 chmod/ACL 都硬；
- 需要 `sudo`（root 权限）执行，且文件系统要支持该属性（ext4/xfs 支持；
  某些网络/容器文件系统不支持）；
- **对 safemode 有副作用**：文件被删后守护插件本可自动重建
  （detectDrift 发现 missing → force 还原），`+i` 会连守护的重建也挡住；
  升级插件、改白名单也都要先 `-i`。所以建议只在"完全不想被任何人动"
  的场景使用，日常用基础只读（attrib/chmod 444）即可。
section: 解锁

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · 三级防护对比：| 方案 | 挡内容修改 | 挡删除 | 挡 root | 需要权限 | 对守护自愈的影响 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attrib +R` / `chmod 444`（基础只读） | ✅ 普通用户 | ❌ | ❌ | 无 | 无（守护一致则不写） |
| icacls deny（ACL） | ✅ | ✅（加 DE） | ❌（管理员可绕） | 文件所有者 | 无 |
| `chattr +i`（immutable） | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | sudo | ⚠️ 挡住守护重建，需先 `-i` |

建议：**日常用基础只读即可**（pnpm 以普通用户运行，444 已完全拦截安装）；
要防误删再加 ACL `(DE)`；只有"这台机器上的任何账号（含 root）都不能动
safemode 配置"才算刚需 chattr +i。
section: 三级防护对比

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · 1. On startup: force-restore (regardless of whether the profile exists or was modified)：Every time DSH boots and loads this plugin row, it unconditionally rewrites
`$DSH_HOME/profiles/safemode/` back to the whitelist template:

| File | Forced content |
|---|---|
| `package.json` | `dsh.profile.bundles` = whitelist (default `@deepseek-ai/dsh-base` + `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app`), `dependencies` emptied |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | empty user patch layer (`[]` template) |
| `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | same pnpm settings as an official profile |
section: 1. On startup: force-restore (regardless of whether the profile exists or was modified)

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · 1. On startup: force-restore (regardless of whether the profile exists or was modified)：If the files already match the template, nothing is written (avoids a
self-triggering watch loop); anything that drifted is rewritten.
section: 1. On startup: force-restore (regardless of whether the profile exists or was modified)

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · 2. At runtime: continuous guard (drift checking)：While the plugin row is alive, two channels watch the profile for modification:

- **fs.watch realtime**: any change to `package.json` / `cordis.patch.yml` /
  `pnpm-workspace.yaml` → debounced 300ms → immediate restore;
- **30s polling fallback**: full `detectDrift()` comparison (covers
  unreliable watch mounts and files replaced wholesale externally).
section: 2. At runtime: continuous guard (drift checking)

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · 2. At runtime: continuous guard (drift checking)：On drift (bundle added/removed, patch layer written to, `dependencies` added)
the guard restores the profile and logs a warning:
`safemode profile was modified (...); restored to whitelist template`.
section: 2. At runtime: continuous guard (drift checking)

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · Hardening: make the three managed files read-only：> ⚠️ **Never lock the whole directory**: DSH rewrites `cordis.yml` on every
> boot (`prepareProfile` unconditionally writeFileSync), so a read-only
> directory or read-only `cordis.yml` makes safemode fail to start (verified:
> exit 1). Windows `attrib +R <dir> /S` recursively locks every file
> including `cordis.yml` — **do not use it**.

```powershell

section: POSIX: the three files to 444 (the directory still needs r-x and must stay writable)

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · POSIX: the three files to 444 (the directory still needs r-x and must stay writable)：Notes:
- **Let the plugin create/restore the profile first, then lock** — the
  content must match the whitelist template before locking (the guard only
  writes when it detects drift; template-matching content is left untouched,
  so locking coexists with the guard). If drift is found while locked, the
  guard's restore fails with a warning — that is the expected behavior of a
  lock: locked means no drift should exist.
- Unlock before changing the whitelist. The guard itself is unaffected — it
  reads `package.json` to detect drift and only writes when a drift is found.
section: POSIX: the three files to 444 (the directory still needs r-x and must stay writable)

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · Deeper protection: ACL (Windows) and chattr +i (Linux)：The `attrib +R` / `chmod 444` above is "**basic read-only**": the two
platforms treat it differently, and neither can stop **deletion** (deleting
a file depends on the parent directory's permissions; root ignores all
permission bits anyway). The following are "**hard locks**", pick as needed:
section: Deeper protection: ACL (Windows) and chattr +i (Linux)

text: dsh-safemode-profile README · Windows: ACL deny (icacls) — precise control over write vs delete：```powershell
section: Windows: ACL deny (icacls) — precise control over write vs delete

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · Deny the current user write access to the three files (W = write data)：icacls "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\safemode\package.json" /deny "$env:USERNAME:(W)"
icacls "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\safemode\cordis.patch.yml" /deny "$env:USERNAME:(W)"
icacls "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\safemode\pnpm-workspace.yaml" /deny "$env:USERNAME:(W)"
section: Deny the current user write access to the three files (W = write data)

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · Stronger: also deny deletion (DE = delete; WD = write data / create file)：icacls "...\package.json" /deny "$env:USERNAME:(WD,DE)"
```

To unlock (remove that user's deny entries):

```powershell
icacls "...\package.json" /remove:d "$env:USERNAME"
```
section: Stronger: also deny deletion (DE = delete; WD = write data / create file)

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · Stronger: also deny deletion (DE = delete; WD = write data / create file)：Key points:
- `(W)` blocks content modification, `(DE)` blocks deletion, `(WD)` blocks
  write + create — more precise than attrib: you can block writes while
  leaving admins able to delete;
- **Still does not stop administrators**: Administrators / SYSTEM have Full
  Control (F) by default and can take ownership or clear the deny. To block
  them too, deny `BUILTIN\Administrators` as well — but admins can still
  bypass via "take ownership";
- icacls requires permission to modify the file's ACL (the file owner has it
  by default).
section: Stronger: also deny deletion (DE = delete; WD = write data / create file)

text: dsh-safemode-profile README · Linux: immutable attribute (chattr +i) — root cannot touch it either：```bash
section: Linux: immutable attribute (chattr +i) — root cannot touch it either

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · Lock: file cannot be modified, deleted, or renamed (root included)：sudo chattr +i ~/.dsh/profiles/safemode/package.json \
              ~/.dsh/profiles/safemode/cordis.patch.yml \
              ~/.dsh/profiles/safemode/pnpm-workspace.yaml
section: Lock: file cannot be modified, deleted, or renamed (root included)

text: dsh-safemode-profile README · Inspect：lsattr ~/.dsh/profiles/safemode/package.json     # output containing "i" = locked
section: Inspect

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · Unlock：sudo chattr -i ~/.dsh/profiles/safemode/package.json \
              ~/.dsh/profiles/safemode/cordis.patch.yml \
              ~/.dsh/profiles/safemode/pnpm-workspace.yaml
```
section: Unlock

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · Unlock：Key points:
- `+i` (immutable) is the strongest lock: **nobody (root included) can
  modify, delete, or rename** — you must `-i` first for any operation,
  harder than chmod or ACL;
- Requires `sudo` (root), and the filesystem must support the attribute
  (ext4/xfs do; some network/container filesystems do not);
- **Side effect for safemode**: the guard normally rebuilds a deleted file
  (detectDrift finds "missing" → force-restore), but `+i` blocks even that;
  upgrading the plugin or changing the whitelist also needs `-i` first. Use
  it only when "no account on this machine (root included) may touch the
  safemode config" is a real requirement; basic read-only
  (attrib / chmod 444) is enough for everyday use.
section: Unlock

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · Three levels compared：| Option | Blocks content edit | Blocks delete | Blocks root | Requires | Impact on guard self-heal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attrib +R` / `chmod 444` (basic) | ✅ for normal users | ❌ | ❌ | none | none (guard skips writes when clean) |
| icacls deny (ACL) | ✅ | ✅ (with DE) | ❌ (admins can bypass) | file owner | none |
| `chattr +i` (immutable) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | sudo | ⚠️ blocks guard rebuild; `-i` first |
section: Three levels compared

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · Three levels compared：Suggestion: **basic read-only is enough for everyday use** (pnpm runs as a
normal user, 444 already blocks installs completely); add ACL `(DE)` if you
want to guard against accidental deletion; only choose `chattr +i` when
"no account (root included) may touch the safemode config" is a hard
requirement.
section: Three levels compared

text:
dsh-safemode-profile README · Notes：- **Port**: safemode also carries the webServer, default 3080. Running it
  alongside the web profile conflicts (`EADDRINUSE` fails the boot) — use
  `--port` to separate them: `dsh --profile safemode --port 3081`.
- **Sessions/credentials are NOT isolated**: sessions, `settings.yaml` and
  `.env` are home-level shared; safemode only isolates plugins.
- **Home patch leaks in**: `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml` applies to every profile
  — don't mount plugins there (the guard only watches the safemode directory
  itself, not the home patch).
- **Don't hand-edit `cordis.yml`**: DSH rewrites it on every boot; edit
  `cordis.patch.yml` instead — but safemode's patch layer is restored to empty
  by this plugin, so customize through the whitelist env var.
section: Notes
